Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 16 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS MoHFW Releases NHA Estimates for India 2023-24, GHE Rose to Rs 4.14 lakh Cr On 15 November 2026, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) released the National Health Accounts (NHA) Estimates for India 2023-24, highlighting that India’s Government Health Expenditure(GHE) rose to Rs 4.14 lakh crore (Cr) in 2023-24 from Rs 1.30 lakh Cr in 2013-14. Exam Hints:  What? Release of NHA Estimates for India 2023–24  Released by: MoHFW  Edition: 11th  Prepared by: NHATS, NHSRC  GHE: Rs 4.14 lakh crore (1.43% of GDP)  Total Health Expenditure: Rs 9.52 lakh crore (3.29% of GDP)  OOPE Share: 42.7% (down from 64.2% in FY2013–14)  Per Capita GHE: Rs 2,959  Primary Healthcare Spending: Rs 1.53 lakh crore. NHA Publication and Framework: Published By: The National Health Accounts (NHA) Estimates are published by the MoHFW. Prepared By: The NHA estimates 2023-24 represent the 11th round of estimates prepared by the National Health Accounts Technical Secretariat (NHATS), located at the National Health Systems Resource Centre (NHSRC), under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Framework: The estimates follow the internationally recognised System of Health Accounts (SHA) 2011 framework, which helps track healthcare expenditure and the flow of funds within the healthcare system. NHA Report 2023-24 Data: Government Health Expenditure (GHE): Between 2013–14 and 2023–24, the government’s share in Total Health Expenditure (THE) increased by 14.9 percentage points, representing nearly 52% growth.  In 2023–24, State Governments contributed approximately 68% of GHE, while the Union Government accounted for 32%.  Per capita GHE increased from Rs 1,042 in 2013–14 to Rs 2,959 in 2023–24, indicating a nearly threefold rise in government spending on healthcare per person.  GHE accounted for 1.43% of India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in 2023–24. Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE): The share of OOPE in THE declined from 64.2% in 2013-14 to 42.7% in 2023-24, registering a fall of 21.5%.  OOPE refers to the money individuals and households pay directly from their own pockets for healthcare services, medicines, tests and treatment. THE: India’s THE stood at Rs 9,52,122 Cr in 2023-24, equivalent to 3.29% of GDP.  The Per capita THE was estimated at Rs 6,801.  This is the average amount spent on healthcare for each person from all sources, including Government expenditure, Private health insurance, Out-of-pocket expenditure. Expenditure Composition: Of the total expenditure:  Current Health Expenditure (CHE) accounted for Rs 8.37 lakh Cr (87.9%)  while Capital Expenditure (CE) stood at Rs 1.15 lakh Cr (12.1%).

Economic Resilience: India’s score improved from 66 points in 2021–25 (third place behind Russia with 74 and China with 71) to 71 points for 2026–30. Growth: India’s real GDP growth is projected at 6.9% during 2026–30, while gross national savings and gross capital formation are estimated at 35.3% and 36.7% of GDP, respectively. India Signs San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity  Under: Pax Silica initiative  Where? Pax Silica Founders Retreat, San Francisco, USA  Convened By: Jacob Helberg, USA Under-Secretary of State for Economic Affairs  Signatories: 10 governments: USA, India, Australia, Israel, Japan, Republic of Korea, Qatar, Singapore, UAE and UK  Purpose: Secure critical technologies and AI supply chains. About the San Francisco Declaration: Declaration: It was launched and signed on 15 November 2026, convened by Jacob Helberg, USA Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs. Participating Countries: The declaration was jointly issued by 10 governments: the USA, India, Australia, Israel, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the United Kingdom (UK). Framework: Established a shared framework to protect sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure for the AI and Super Intelligence (SI) era, recognising economic security as national security and promoting coordinated action against economic coercion, supply-chain disruptions and unfair market practices. Technologies: Covers software, materials, technical knowledge, components and manufacturing capabilities essential to AI and Super Intelligence (SI) supply chains, protecting against theft, illicit transfers and hostile acquisition that could threaten economic and national security. Infrastructure: Covers ports, transport and logistics networks, communications, energy systems and digital platforms, protecting them from disruptions, hostile control and unauthorised data exposure. Resilience: Calls for diversified and trusted supply chains to reduce excessive dependencies, strengthen economic resilience and protect strategic technological capabilities. Working Groups: Proposed five working groups focusing on pro-innovation policy frameworks, Super Intelligence (SI) adoption, supply-chain cooperation, security hubs and SI security to translate shared commitments into coordinated action. About Pax Silica: Launch: Pax Silica was launched in December 2025 by Jacob Helberg as the United States Department of State’s flagship initiative focused on AI and supply-chain security. Objectives: Aims to strengthen cooperation among partner countries across critical minerals, energy inputs, advanced manufacturing, semiconductors and AI infrastructure, building resilient and trusted supply chains amid growing technological competition and economic pressure involving China. Accession: India formally joined Pax Silica on 20 February 2026 during the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi, Delhi, strengthening its participation in trusted global semiconductor and AI manufacturing ecosystems.
